title: Accelerating DTCO with a Sample-Efficient Active Learning Framework for TCAD Device Modeling
problem: Neural Compact Models require substantial training data, and TCAD simulations are time-intensive and expensive. The challenge is to accurately model device behavior while minimizing the number of required TCAD simulations.
motivation: Accelerating DTCO through efficient device modeling reduces design time and cost, enabling faster chip design optimization.
method: The framework employs an active learning approach with a ranking algorithm that evaluates multiple metrics including expected variance from the neural tangent kernel (NTK), TCAD simulation time, and I-V curve complexity. This intelligent selection strategy identifies the most informative simulation points to run, reducing the total number of simulations needed while maintaining model accuracy.
key_novelty: Using neural tangent kernel-based variance estimation within an active learning framework to intelligently select the most informative device simulations, significantly reducing the sample complexity of TCAD-based device modeling.
contributions: Active Learning framework for reducing simulation count in NCM-based device modeling
Ranking algorithm combining NTK variance, simulation time, and I-V curve complexity metrics
28.5% MSE improvement within 30-minute time budget for device modeling
86.7% reduction in data points required for ring oscillator process optimization
